newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo to import cement after factory break down.
newsitem.headline: Congo to import cement after factory break down.

text.p: Congo is to import cement for a limited period following the breakdown of the machinery powering its only cement works, officials said at the weekend.
Repairs on main motor at the Societe Cimentiere du Congo factory at Loutete 150 km (90 miles) south of Brazzaville were expected to take more than three months, they added.
The machinery had been sent to Zaire for repairs, they said.
SOCICO, half-owned by the government and half by Norwegian firm Scancem, has an annual capacity of 250,000 tonnes.

The Congolese government, in common with many governments in Africa, is looking to sell off its interest in a range of companies in line with economic liberalisation policies promoted by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund.
In August, it invited Chinese investors to take a stake in the company during a meeting of a joint-commission bringing together officials and businessmen from the two countries.
Officials say South African Company Pretoria Portland Cement is also interested in taking a stake.
